prompt:
阅读下面这份虚构的社区共享书屋试运营记录，仅依据材料回答文末问题。

【背景与目标】
青禾社区把一间闲置活动室改成共享书屋，试运营从四月持续到六月。书屋主要面向附近居民、周边小学的家庭和白天在家工作的年轻人。项目希望提供安静阅读空间，也让闲置图书重新流通。负责人明确表示，试运营不追求借阅量排名，而是判断开放时间、管理成本和居民需求能否长期匹配。书屋没有付费会员，居民凭登记卡借书，每次最多借三本，期限为十四天。

【空间与服务】
房间分成安静阅读区、儿童阅读区和借还书台。安静区有十二个座位，儿童区有六张矮凳。入口设置归还箱，闭馆时仍可还书，但工作人员要在下次开馆后核对书号才能销账。居民捐赠的旧书先检查破损和重复情况，再决定上架、交换或者回收。旧杂志放在单独的交换架，不计入可借馆藏。公告栏展示活动时间和常见问题，不公布借阅人的姓名。

【四月的观察】
最初开放时间为周二至周五下午两点到六点，周末上午九点到下午五点。四月登记了九十名借阅人，借出一百八十册图书。问卷显示，上班族希望工作日晚间也能进入书屋；带孩子的家庭更关心周末能否找到座位。志愿者发现，借阅高峰集中在周六下午，而周三下午经常只有少量读者。部分居民把未登记的书直接放入归还箱，增加了核对时间。

【五月的调整】
管理组将周三下午改成周三晚上六点至九点，其他时间保持不变，并给归还箱增加填写书号的小卡片。五月登记人数累计达到一百四十人，当月借出二百六十册。晚间开放吸引了此前难以到场的上班族，但两名志愿者无法长期承担晚班，因此排班仍不稳定。儿童故事会每两周一次，每次最多十二组家庭，报名不收费。故事会期间儿童区较吵，有读者建议使用隔音帘，但消防通道不能被遮挡。

【六月的反馈】
六月当月借出二百四十册，略低于五月。两次周末暴雨导致临时闭馆，不能仅凭借阅量下降认定调整失败。归还箱小卡片减少了无法确认书号的情况，但仍有读者忘记填写。问卷收回六十八份，其中四十二份支持保留晚间开放，十六份希望增加周日上午活动，十份没有明确意见。问卷只覆盖愿意填写的到访者，管理组提醒不能把它当作全社区所有居民的投票。

【预算与人员】
三个月场地免租，水电和清洁支出合计一千二百元，登记卡、标签及文具支出三百元。书架由居民捐赠，未计购买成本。下季度社区可提供两千元固定补助，优先用于水电、清洁和安全用品。是否采购隔音帘尚未决定，需要先评估消防和清洁要求。共有八名志愿者登记，但能稳定每周服务的只有五名。负责人建议先明确班次替补，再考虑增加开放时段。

【尚未解决的问题】
纸质登记表查找较慢，管理组正在比较电子表格和简单的借阅系统。电子化必须限制访问权限，避免在公开群里传播居民电话。工作人员也不希望为处理少量逾期书而收集更多个人信息。有人建议开展图书交换日，但目前没有额外人手负责整理。项目组计划在七月底复盘晚间到访量、每班所需人时和归还登记错误，之后再决定是否扩大服务。

【统计口径】
借阅量按完成登记的册数计算，同一本书被不同读者借走会分别计数；它不等于独立读者人数。到场阅读但没有借书的人尚未完整统计。四月与五月的登记人数是累计值，而月度借阅量是当月值，不能把两类数字直接相除后称为所有居民的使用率。活动报名人数与实际到场人数也可能不同。

【居民建议与实施条件】
部分家长愿意参与周末整理，但只能不定期到场。附近学校提出交换阅读推荐清单，尚未安排教师值班。管理组认为这些支持值得尝试，却不能代替固定排班。另有居民建议取消逾期提醒以减少工作，负责人担心图书长期不归还会影响其他读者，提出先用温和提醒并观察效果。任何新活动都应事先明确负责收尾的人。

【异常处理】
若出现漏水或电源故障，值班员先暂停受影响区域，再联系物业。儿童活动需要监护人陪同，志愿者不承担托管职责。下季度评估时，应单独记录临时闭馆时段，以便解释借阅量的变化。

请用中文概括三个方面：已经证实的服务改善、现有证据的局限、下季度最应优先解决的事项。说明理由，不把建议写成已经完成的工作。

以下是虚构的城市资料馆改造会议记录。请根据全文检索事实，回答最后的问题；材料没有说明的事项请写“未确定”。

【一月八日：立项】
资料馆计划把二层储物间改成供公众使用的地方史阅览室，项目代号“溪桥”。项目联系人是陈岚，档案修复由周越负责，网络和预约系统由林舟负责。公众区设在二层东侧，西侧仍为工作人员整理区。馆长要求施工时保留一楼正常借阅服务，不能把通往楼梯的走廊用于存放材料。项目原计划六月开放，具体日期须通过验收后公布。

【一月二十二日：空间讨论】
设计方提出十四个阅读座位，其中两个座位预留更宽的轮椅通行空间。纸质地方志只能在室内阅读，复制申请需工作人员审核。居民捐赠的照片先扫描，原件在取得书面同意后才决定是否保管。会议讨论了带锁储物柜，但尚未确认采购数量。工作人员入口与公众入口分开，紧急出口维持原有位置。门口拟设置预约二维码，同时保留电话预约方式。

【二月六日：设备比选】
扫描仪有甲、乙两种方案。甲方案价格较低，适合一般文件；乙方案可以减少脆弱纸张被压平的次数，但需要更宽的桌面。修复组建议试用旧报纸后再决定，没有当场选择供应商。照明方案采用可调亮度灯具，避免读者座位直接照射馆藏。空调控制器计划安装在工作人员区域，由值班员统一调节，不允许读者自行修改设置。

【二月二十日：预算调整】
项目总预算最初为十八万元，因电路改造增加两万元，修订后总额为二十万元。新增费用优先保障电路与消防，不用于新增座位。财务要求把设备采购、施工和长期维护分别记账，不能把志愿者服务时长折算成已支付的工资。三家供应商的报价都包含运输，但只有其中两家提供一年上门维护，因此不能只按设备标价比较。会议没有确定最终中标单位。

【三月四日：施工安排】
施工队计划周一闭馆日进行噪声较大的钻孔作业，其他工作日在开馆前搬运材料。二层东侧临时封闭，一楼读者可继续使用原来的阅览桌。所有旧电线拆除前先拍照编号，避免把仍在使用的设备线路误拆。馆方指定陈岚汇总每周进度，但现场安全检查由施工负责人执行。消防验收需要在家具定位完成之后进行，不能仅凭电路测试通过就宣布可以开放。

【三月十九日：试用规则】
预约每场九十分钟，每场最多十二人，保留两个座位供行动不便或临时需要帮助的读者。资料馆决定试用期不收取预约费用，取消预约应尽量提前通知。迟到十五分钟后，工作人员可以释放预约名额。读者可自带笔记本电脑，但不得给设备拍摄可识别他人的借阅信息。是否允许个人手机拍摄馆藏内容，要依据资料授权情况逐件判断。

【四月二日：进度复核】
电路改造完成，家具尚未全部到货，扫描仪仍在试用。修复组发现部分旧报纸纸张比预期更脆，需要额外培训两名工作人员。预约系统已经能接收申请，但短信提醒尚未启用。负责人再次强调六月只是计划开放月份，验收结果和培训完成情况都可能影响日期。宣传组暂时只发布项目介绍，不公布首场预约链接，也不承诺试运营期间可以提供全部馆藏。

【四月十六日：后续事项】
下一次现场复核定在五月九日上午，由陈岚协调各组到场。林舟负责在复核前完成预约系统的权限检查，周越负责准备旧报纸操作示范。馆方希望开放后的首月分别记录到访人数、取消预约次数和工作人员辅助时长，避免用单一到访量评价服务。纸质馆藏是否可以外借并未重新讨论，仍执行前述室内阅读规则。

【档案整理说明】
现有资料按街道和年代建立索引，重复版本保留来源说明，不直接丢弃。修复组将严重破损的原件先放入隔离盒，扫描目录标记为暂不可查阅。新整理的资料需要另一名工作人员核对页码，再纳入公众检索。志愿者可以整理公开目录，不能独自接触未授权的私人信件。

【复核准备】
各组应把已完成事项和待办事项分开提交，验收表由馆方统一保存。宣传图片只拍摄已整理的公众空间，不能因为桌椅已经摆放就暗示全部工程完成。试用设备的运行记录也要保留，以便在采购决定前比较实际效果。

请按编号回答：1. 项目代号与联系人是什么？2. 修订后总预算多少，增加部分用于什么？3. 每场预约多久、最多多少人？4. 下一次现场复核何时举行？5. 已确定最终扫描仪供应商和具体开放日期了吗？

请依据以下虚构的产品团队交接材料制定下一阶段计划。材料中的决定、建议和未完成工作需要区分，不要自行添加人手或预算。

【产品与用户】
“路灯”是一款给小型维修团队使用的工单工具，支持客户报修、派单、上门记录和完工确认。团队服务三十家商户，当前试用客户集中在同一城区。客户最在意的是收到明确的到场时间，其次才是界面外观。管理员通过网页派单，维修人员主要使用手机查看任务。网络不稳定时，维修人员会先在纸上记录，晚上回到办公室补录，容易遗漏现场照片和零件数量。

【已有功能】
网页端可以新增工单、分配负责人、筛选状态和导出月报。手机端只能查看任务与上传照片，还不能离线保存文字。客户会在工单创建和完成时收到通知，派单改期目前不会自动通知。系统保存每次状态变更的时间和操作者，但导出的月报只显示最后一次状态。历史工单不能由普通维修人员删除，管理员也必须填写删除原因。试用环境每天夜间备份一次，最近一次恢复演练在两个月前完成。

【一周内收到的反馈】
东街维修队认为改期通知最紧急，因为客户会按照原约定时间等待。西桥维修队遇到地下室信号差，要求增加离线备注；他们表示照片可以回到有网络的地方再传。南园管理员认为月报数字与手工表格不同，怀疑跨月完成的工单被算错。产品经理已经确认存在统计口径不一致，但还没有证实数据库丢失记录。两家新客户询问是否能接入付款功能，团队尚未承诺开发时间。

【故障与风险】
上周出现过两次重复通知，日志显示同一任务重试后没有检查通知是否已发送。没有证据表明工单被重复创建。另一项风险是部分旧账号仍拥有过宽的导出权限，可能看到其他维修队的客户电话。安全负责人要求本阶段先收紧权限，并保留操作记录。手机离线功能可能引入覆盖新数据的问题，设计时必须说明冲突如何处理，不能简单用最后上传的记录覆盖所有字段。

【人员与时间】
下一阶段共两周，十个工作日。团队有一名后端工程师、一名前端工程师和一名测试工程师，每人每天有效研发时间按六小时估算。产品经理可在第一、第三和第八个工作日组织半小时评审。后端工程师第二周周三请假一天。测试工程师除项目测试外，每天还需一小时处理现有客户问题，这一小时从六小时中扣除。不得临时增加外包，也不能安排周末加班。

【已有估算】
权限收紧与审计检查预计后端两天、测试一天；通知去重预计后端一天、测试半天。改期通知预计后端一天、前端一天、测试一天。月报口径确认预计产品经理与客户协商后才能确定，修改实现预计后端一天、前端半天、测试一天。离线文字备注预计前端四天、后端两天、测试两天，但估算尚未包含复杂冲突处理。付款功能没有可靠估算，不应为了凑齐计划直接承诺上线。

【发布条件】
本阶段最多安排一次正式发布。发布前必须完成权限检查、通知重试验证和至少一次备份恢复演练。恢复演练需要后端与测试共同参与半天，可使用已有测试环境，但不能操作真实客户数据。测试环境与正式环境的配置变更要留存对照表。功能可以通过开关逐步启用，发生严重问题时先关闭新增功能，再根据变更记录判断是否回滚，不得先删除日志来节约空间。

【交接补充】
客户成功同事可以帮助收集月报样例，但无法代替产品经理决定统计口径。离线备注可以先安排方案验证，验证结果用于下阶段估算，不一定要在本阶段完整上线。团队希望在第八个工作日进行发布准备评审，最后两个工作日用于处理缺陷和观察。项目结束后，应分别记录工单处理效率、通知错误数量和用户反馈，不将新增功能数量作为唯一成功标准。

【依赖确认补充】
通知去重与改期通知共用发送模块，前者应先完成接口约定，再由前端接入改期操作。月报页面可以先展示口径说明，但最终计算规则必须经产品经理确认。安全检查中发现的权限问题需要覆盖已有账号和新建账号，不能只验证新注册流程。测试工程师希望每项任务至少提前一天提供可验证版本。

【沟通安排】
第一天由产品经理集中说明取舍，避免不同客户收到相互矛盾的承诺。任何延期都要说明影响和替代办法。客户反馈记录保留问题原文，但讨论材料应隐藏电话号码。结项汇报须分别列出已经上线、仅完成验证和留待后续三类事项。

请给出可执行的两周计划：先说明优先级，再列出主要任务、负责人、依赖关系、验证方式和暂缓事项。检查人时是否冲突，说明离线功能是否应在本阶段承诺完整上线。

Read the following fictional operations review and answer the question at the end. Base your analysis on the supplied evidence and distinguish observations from proposals.

Harbor Tools lends equipment to neighborhood repair groups. Its depot serves residents who need a drill, ladder, sewing machine, or similar item for a short project. The service began with donated equipment and now uses a modest annual grant. Members reserve items online or by telephone. Most loans last three days. Staff inspect returned equipment before marking it available again, so an item being physically present does not always mean that it is ready for another loan.

During the first quarter, the depot opened on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday mornings. Records showed that Saturday was the busiest session, but the team did not record how many people visited without borrowing anything. A survey of current members asked whether longer opening hours would help. Many respondents supported an evening session. The survey did not reach people who had never registered, and the coordinator cautioned that it could not represent every household in the area.

In April, the team replaced Thursday morning with Thursday evening. Total loans rose from 180 in March to 225 in April. However, April also included a publicity event and the arrival of several donated power tools. Staff therefore could not attribute the entire increase to evening opening. The evening session was popular with people returning from work, while two regular morning visitors said the new schedule was less convenient. Telephone reservations remained available during the original office hours.

The reservation system allows a member to request an item that has not yet passed inspection. Such requests are marked pending and should not generate a collection notice. In May, three members received notices too early because an operator selected the wrong status. No injuries were reported, and none of the uninspected items left the depot. The coordinator proposed a separate inspection checklist and clearer labels. The proposed changes had not been implemented when this review was written.

Maintenance records show that ladders and electric sanders take longer to inspect than hand tools. One volunteer can check simple tools, but electrical repairs require an external technician. The technician visits twice a month. A broken drill can therefore remain unavailable for several weeks even when replacement parts are inexpensive. Staff suggested keeping one spare for frequently requested items, but the storage room is nearly full. Buying more equipment without changing storage or maintenance arrangements may not reduce waiting times.

The team has six registered volunteers. Only four can cover a regular weekly shift, and two of those four will be away for part of August. Paid staff can support administration but cannot supervise an additional public session without reducing time spent on inspections. Training a new volunteer takes two supervised sessions. No budget has been approved for extra paid hours. The coordinator wants the next plan to account for these limits before advertising any expansion.

For the next quarter, the available operating budget is 2,400 units. Rent and utilities require 1,200, routine technician visits require 600, and essential safety supplies require 200. The remaining amount may cover small repairs or approved experiments. A suggested new booking system would cost 900 before training and data migration. Its supplier claims it would reduce administrative work, but the team has not tested that claim. The current system can export records, although older entries contain inconsistent item names.

Several members have asked for more predictable collection times rather than a larger catalog. One repair group offered to label storage shelves during a closed session. Another offered to run a demonstration day, but that event would need supervision and could interrupt normal lending. The coordinator recommended testing shelf labels and the inspection checklist first. She also asked for separate counts of reservations, completed loans, cancellations, inspection delays, and visits without a loan, so that a change in one measure would not be mistaken for an improvement in all of them.

Any trial should preserve telephone access for members who cannot use the website. Personal contact details must remain accessible only to staff who need them. The depot already keeps a daily backup, but it has not recently checked whether the export can be restored. Before changing software, staff would need a recovery test and a clear method for matching old item names to new records. The depot also needs a way to stop a trial that increases errors. Staff proposed a short review after two evening sessions, with one person responsible for collecting incident notes. A quiet week would not by itself prove that a change was safe: the review should consider the number of loans handled. If volunteers become unavailable, existing reservations should be contacted before any public opening hours are reduced.

Recommend a practical next-quarter plan in English. Explain what the loan increase does and does not establish, identify the most urgent operational risks, prioritize actions within the stated staffing and budget limits, and name the measurements needed to decide whether the trials worked.

category: 长上下文·英文数学核算
prompt:
Read this fictional workshop ledger and answer in English. Use only the stated accounting rules. Show the calculations, distinguish paid tickets from people who attended, and do not count an unpaid promise as cash received.

Program and tickets
River Print held three weekend classes. A ticket covers one participant and one materials kit. Accompanying adults who do not make a print need no ticket or kit. Helpers are volunteers, not paying participants. Prices already include all discounts. Each reservation was paid before the event, and the refunds below were completed before closing the ledger.
Class A sold 24 tickets at 80 credits each. Three tickets were refunded in full; 19 people attended.
Class B sold 18 tickets at 100 credits each. Two tickets were refunded in full; 15 people attended.
Class C sold 20 tickets at 60 credits each. One ticket was refunded in full; 17 people attended.
There were no tickets sold at the door. People who kept a valid ticket but did not attend received no refund and consumed no kit. Do not add companions or volunteers to attendance.

Other receipts
A local shop donated 500 credits, already received. Another company promised 300 credits after receiving photographs, but has paid nothing. Treat the received donation as income and the unpaid promise as a note only. The organizer contributed a temporary 400-credit loan so supplies could be bought. This is financing, not workshop income, and the exercise does not ask you to calculate the bank balance or loan repayment.

Materials and inventory
The organizer purchased 70 identical kits for 12 credits each, paying 840 credits before the classes. Count one kit for each actual attendee. Three additional kits were used for demonstrations, and two unopened kits were damaged and discarded. Charge those five kits to this event as well. All remaining kits are usable stock for a future event, valued at the same unit price; their purchase is not automatically a cost of this event.
Paper purchased specifically for the three classes cost 90 credits and was entirely consumed. A donated stack of practice paper has no assigned value in this exercise and must not be priced using an outside estimate. Finished prints belong to attendees and are not saleable inventory.

Venue, services, and fees
The venue charge was 180 credits per day for two days. The instructor was paid 450 credits in total, covering preparation and all three classes. Cleaning cost 60 credits. The ticket platform charges 2 percent of ticket receipts remaining after refunds. It charges nothing on donations or loans and returned all fees related to refunded tickets. No other charge, tax, payment fee, or compensation is included.
A 200-credit venue deposit was returned in full after inspection. It is neither income nor an event cost. A reusable drying rack was borrowed without charge and returned undamaged. Do not invent depreciation for borrowed equipment.

Checks and supporting notes
The attendance lists count each participant once within the relevant class. Nobody attended more than one class. Staff initially wrote the number of reservations beside the materials issue column; the corrected signed issue sheet matches actual attendance. Use that correction, not the earlier shorthand. Receipts confirm that the stated instructor and cleaning amounts are totals rather than rates per class.
The stock cupboard was counted after demonstrations and damage disposal. No kits were given to volunteers, and no unused kits were transferred to another project before the count. The organizer wants event income and event cost, not all movements of money during the week. In particular, buying supplies, receiving a loan, and returning a deposit must not be combined into a misleading profit calculation.
Retain full precision in intermediate calculations. Show monetary totals to two decimal places, attendance percentage to one decimal place, and cost per attendee to two decimal places. Identify which denominator you use for attendance.

Stock reconciliation
Opening kit inventory was zero. Reconcile purchases against attendee use, demonstrations, damage, and closing stock. Demonstration kits must not also be included in attendee use. If the quantities do not balance, identify the discrepancy instead of changing a source number. The treasurer needs this reconciliation to order supplies for the next workshop, separately from the event surplus.

Questions
Calculate valid paid tickets after refunds, total attendance, retained ticket receipts, platform fee, recognized income, consumed kit cost, closing kit inventory, total event cost, and event surplus. Then calculate attendance as a percentage of valid tickets and event cost per attendee. Explain the numerical effect on the surplus of charging the entire 840-credit kit purchase to this event. Finally identify two cash movements that must be excluded from event income and explain why.

阅读下面虚构的离线目录同步需求和 Python 实现，找出问题并修复。只使用 Python 标准库，不需要数据库、网络访问或线程。

【数据结构】
state 是调用者长期保存的字典，包含 cursor 和 items。cursor 是最后成功提交的事件序号，初始为零；items 用商品编号作键，每项包含 revision、name、active。page 是一页按 seq 严格递增排列的事件。事件可以是 upsert 或 delete；upsert 提供完整的新版本字段，delete 只将商品标记为 inactive，不从字典删除。所有测试商品和名称都是虚构的。

【提交语义】
一次调用必须是原子的：整页成功后才返回新 state，调用者再替换旧 state；任何事件格式错误都应抛出 ValueError，且原 state 及其嵌套 items 完全不变。不得一边处理一边修改传入对象。返回的新 items 中的记录也不能与旧 state 共用可变字典，否则后续修改会污染旧快照。空页返回等值但相互独立的状态。

【序号与版本】
seq 不大于传入 cursor 的事件是已经提交的重放，只需跳过；正常重放仍有 seq 字段。本页剩余事件先检查格式，再处理。seq 必须是正整数，bool 不能冒充整数。revision 也必须是非负整数。某个合法事件的 revision 不高于该商品当前版本时，不修改商品，但该事件已经成功消费，cursor 仍可推进到它的 seq。不得用最大的商品 revision 代替全局事件 cursor。

【删除约定】
删除未知商品时，也建立一条 tombstone 记录：保留该事件的 revision，name 为 null，active 为 false。之后只有更高 revision 的 upsert 才能重新激活。删除已知商品时保留其 name，只更新 revision 和 active。输入页承诺 seq 有序且不重复，但可能含过期商品版本；函数无需自行排序，也不要忽略格式错误。upsert 的 name 必须是非空字符串，不能把数字强行转换成字符串。

当前实现：
```python
def apply_page(state, page):
    result = dict(state)
    for event in page:
        seq = event['seq']
        if seq <= result['cursor']:
            continue
        result['cursor'] = seq
        item_id = event['id']
        old = result['items'].get(item_id)
        if old and event['revision'] <= old['revision']:
            continue
        if event['op'] == 'delete':
            if old:
                old['active'] = False
        else:
            result['items'][item_id] = {
                'revision': event['revision'],
                'name': str(event['name']),
                'active': True,
            }
    return result
```

【最小现场记录】
原状态 cursor=4，商品 A 的 revision=2、name='灯罩'、active=true。新页含 seq=5 的 A revision=3 删除，随后是 seq=6 的 B upsert，但 B 缺少 name。现有函数处理第二条时抛出异常，调用者发现旧状态中的 A 却已被改成 inactive，无法继续作为重试起点。另一个页面只有对未知商品 C 的 revision=5 删除；当前实现返回后没有保存 C 的版本信息，后续 revision=4 的 upsert 错误地让 C 出现。

【接口约束】
函数签名保持 apply_page(state, page)，返回普通字典。item id 必须是非空字符串，op 只能为 upsert 或 delete。输入 state 可视为符合约定，重点验证尚未消费的事件。缺字段与字段类型不正确都转换为明确的 ValueError，不静默吞掉异常。异常消息要能指出事件序号或出错字段，便于调用者记录。不要为兼容旧错误行为而接受其他 op。

【补充测试要求】
还要检查已经存在的删除标记遇到较旧的 upsert 时不会重新出现。空页面应正常返回且游标不动，重复调用同一有效页面应得到相同业务状态。发生异常后，不仅原字典的顶层键保持原值，其内部每个条目也必须保持原值。不要通过修改测试输入来掩盖失败，也不要用全局变量保存游标；每个 state 都应能独立处理自己的页面。

请给出修复后的完整函数，并写出三个可直接运行的断言测试，至少覆盖整页失败不污染旧状态、未知商品 tombstone 防止旧版本复活，以及重放与过期版本的 cursor 处理。最后简要说明主要错误和修复思路。

请将下面虚构软件的说明翻译成自然、准确的中文，保留标题和编号。必须区分 already available、planned、may 与 must，不把计划中的功能翻译成已经实现。产品名 Harbor Notes、文件扩展名及数值保持不变。译文后解释 checkpoint、conflict copy、read-only 三个术语。

Harbor Notes: Moving a Shared Notebook Between Computers

1. What the package contains
A notebook package contains text pages, attachment references, and a small index. The index helps the application find a page quickly; it is not a second copy of the page content. A package can be opened without an internet connection if its attachments have already been downloaded. Links to attachments stored only on another computer will remain visible, but their contents will not become available merely because the notebook index was copied.

2. Before making a copy
Ask other editors to finish their current edits and close the notebook. Then choose Create Checkpoint from the File menu. This command writes the current notebook contents to a new .hnp file and records the time at which the operation completed. It does not include unsaved changes in another editor's window. For that reason, a checkpoint should not be described as an automatic backup of every change made anywhere in the team.

3. Copying and opening
Copy the .hnp file to a local folder on the destination computer before opening it. Opening a package directly from a removable drive is supported for reading, but saving changes to an unreliable connection may fail. The application checks the index when it opens a package. If the check finds an inconsistency, it offers to rebuild the index from the pages. Rebuilding an index does not recover a page that was never included in the package.

4. Handling conflicts
When a page with the same identifier has been edited on two computers, Harbor Notes preserves both versions and creates a conflict copy. Neither version is automatically declared correct. The editor must compare the contents, merge any required changes, and mark the conflict as resolved. The time shown beside a page is useful context, but a later timestamp alone does not prove that a page contains all changes from an earlier version.

5. Permissions and shared folders
A notebook opened in read-only mode can be searched and exported, but its pages cannot be changed in that session. Read-only mode is an application setting, not a guarantee that nobody else can modify the file through another program. Team administrators should also configure the shared folder's permissions. A person who can read a package may be able to read any private text included in it, even when the application hides that text from its normal navigation panel.

6. Storage and cleanup
The application warns when less than 200 MB of free space remains in the destination folder. This is a warning threshold rather than the exact space required by every notebook. Large attachments may require considerably more space. Do not delete the source package until the destination copy has opened successfully and the team has checked several important pages and attachments. Keep the previous checkpoint until the next agreed review, so that a mistaken merge can still be investigated.

7. Recovery checks
A successful copy operation confirms that bytes were transferred; it does not by itself confirm that the right notebook was selected. During a recovery check, verify the notebook name, checkpoint time, page count, and two sample attachments. Record the result in the team's maintenance log. If a sample attachment is missing, note whether it was absent from the source package or failed during transfer. Those two cases require different follow-up actions.

8. Planned improvements
The current release can export a list of unresolved conflicts. A later release is planned to provide a guided comparison view, but no release date has been announced. The team is also considering optional background synchronization. If introduced, synchronization may reduce manual copying, but it would not remove the need for permission checks or recovery testing. Instructions for features that are still being considered must not be presented as steps available in the current version.

9. Support requests
When reporting a problem, include the application version and the action that failed. Send an anonymized example if possible. Support staff do not need passwords, complete customer notebooks, or unrelated personal files to investigate an index warning. If the problem occurs only with a particular attachment, describe its type and approximate size before deciding whether a copy is necessary.

10. Handover between shifts
Before another editor takes over, close the notebook and record which package is the current working copy. A filename containing the word final is not enough to identify it. The handover note should include the folder, checkpoint time, and any unresolved conflicts. If the next editor cannot open the package, keep the last working copy and contact the person responsible for the handover. Do not create several unrelated replacement notebooks and assume they will merge automatically.

category: 长上下文·英文方案比较
prompt:
Read this fictional procurement brief and recommend a trial plan in English. Prices and product claims are facts of this exercise, not descriptions of real vendors. Separate verified features from promises, calculate costs using the same scope, and do not assume a missing capability exists.

The organization
A small local museum needs a booking system for guided visits. It opens five days a week. School groups usually arrive on weekday mornings, while individuals book most weekend slots. Two reception computers share the task. Staff rotate between the desk and the exhibition rooms, and the museum has no full-time technician. A part-time administrator is available one day a week.
Internet access sometimes disappears for half an hour. During an outage, reception must be able to read the complete list of confirmed visits for that day and record arrivals. New reservations may be written on paper and entered after service returns. The museum does not require new online sales during an outage.

Mandatory conditions
The first-year spending limit is 2,400 credits, including required installation, training, and subscription charges. Existing computers are suitable for every option, so no hardware purchase is needed. Complete booking records must be exportable in a documented, machine-readable format. The museum must retain control of its data if the contract ends.
Daily booking capacity must not be oversold when paper entries are reconciled. Staff need an audit trail explaining manual changes. A public link must not expose visitor telephone numbers. A written agreement defining support and recovery responsibilities is required before purchase.

Option Cedar
Cedar costs 120 credits per month. Installation costs 300 credits and a required introductory training session costs 150 credits. Its trial demonstrated downloading the complete day's confirmed list and recording arrivals while offline. On reconnection, it shows a reconciliation screen that staff must approve before manual bookings become final.
The trial also produced a CSV export containing all booking fields and a separate log of changes. The museum checked both files. Its public pages omit contact details. Email support is included on working days, but an exact response time is not promised. The proposed agreement assigns backup operation to the vendor and monthly export checks to the administrator.

Option Harbor
Harbor costs 80 credits per month, with free installation and a required 100-credit training session. In its demonstration, booking management stopped when the network was disconnected. A cached screen could show the last page viewed, but neither the complete daily list nor offline arrival recording was available.
The vendor plans to add offline support next quarter. The feature is absent from the current written offer and no release date is guaranteed. CSV export and an audit log were demonstrated. Public pages omit contact details, and working-day email support is included. Do not treat the planned offline feature as already delivered.

Option Pine
Pine requires a one-time 1,200-credit license, 250 credits for installation, and a 300-credit annual support agreement. Initial training is included. A demonstration confirmed that daily lists and arrival recording work without the internet.
The demo exported a PDF summary showing visitor names and counts. The vendor says that a complete machine-readable export can be added, but has supplied neither a sample file nor a delivery commitment. Staff could edit bookings, but the test account could not open a change history. The vendor has not clarified whether this is a permission setting or a missing audit feature. Treat both matters as unresolved.

Trial resources
The administrator can spend at most eight hours on a trial next month. Reception can contribute two people for one hour each. The director authorizes fictional visitor records only; production data must remain in the current spreadsheet until the trial succeeds. No vendor is entitled to a purchase just because a trial has started.
Available scenarios include a network outage, conflicting paper bookings, a correction to a visitor count, a cancelled group, an export followed by a restore, and checking the public page from an unauthenticated browser. The trial should test requirements that matter to this museum rather than compare the number of menu items.
Annual support is charged once in the first year; do not multiply it by twelve. All prices exclude no additional mandatory fee for this exercise. Optional customization has no quoted price and cannot be assumed free.

An option that fails today may be reviewed later. That possibility does not justify paying a deposit now or transferring production records into an unproven system.

Task
Compute the known first-year cost of each option. For each, distinguish a demonstrated failure of a mandatory condition from an unresolved claim. Recommend one option to trial first, give a trial schedule within the available staff time, and list three specific questions to settle before signing. If a product cannot yet be approved, explain what evidence would change that judgment.

category: 长上下文·英文事件排序
prompt:
Read the following fictional incident handover and answer in English. Records are deliberately out of order. Reconstruct the sequence using the event timestamps, distinguish a successful download from a correct display, and keep the two affected screens separate.

System background
A museum publishes exhibition schedules to an entrance screen and four gallery screens. Editors prepare a numbered package, obtain approval, and publish it to a server. Each screen checks for updates periodically. A downloaded package is verified before activation. If activation fails, the screen may continue showing the previous package. A device can therefore be online and still display old information.
Reception also keeps a manual observation sheet. Its timestamps indicate when someone looked at a screen, not when the server changed. All times below use the same timezone. Dates must be retained when crossing midnight.

Records
E01, October 9 at 08:10: Reception reports that the entrance screen and west gallery screen still show package 40. The remaining screens show package 41. The observation was made in person, and photographs include the package numbers.

E02, October 8 at 16:20: The editor submits package 41. It moves the first guided visit from 10:00 to 10:30. No other scheduled visit changes. Package 40 remains approved for use until the replacement is activated.

E03, October 9 at 09:05: A technician manually restarts the entrance display service. Its local activation log then confirms package 41, and reception photographs the new 10:30 start time. No action has yet been taken on the west gallery screen.

E04, October 8 at 17:00: The manager approves package 41, and the server publishes it at 17:02. The publication record identifies the approved package checksum and the editor account.

E05, October 8 at 23:48: The entrance screen acknowledges downloading package 41 and passing its checksum check. At 23:49 its activation worker records a lock-file error. Its player continues using package 40. The device heartbeat remains normal.

E06, October 9 at 09:30: The west gallery screen passes a short connectivity test. This establishes network access at the time of the test. No overnight network trace is retained, so the technician cannot infer continuous overnight connectivity.

E07, October 9 at 08:25: Reception puts up a temporary printed notice at the entrance giving the correct 10:30 time. This is a visitor-facing mitigation, not a software repair.

E08, October 8 at 18:10: The three unaffected gallery screens report successful activation of package 41. The west screen has a normal heartbeat at 18:12, but its update log contains no package 41 download acknowledgement.

E09, October 9 at 10:00: The technician discovers that the west screen's update task is disabled in its local configuration. The configuration file was last changed on October 7, but the retained record does not identify who changed it or why. There is no evidence that the editor disabled the task.

E10, October 9 at 10:20: After approval, the technician enables the west update task. The screen downloads and activates package 41. At 10:24 reception photographs the correct display. The entrance screen still shows package 41 during the same check.

E11, October 9 at 11:00: A vendor email suggests that a brief network outage might explain both screens. It supplies no device logs or timestamps. Treat this as a proposed explanation, not a verified finding.

Handover requirements
The director wants a concise account that a colleague can verify from record IDs. Separate package preparation, approval, publication, download, activation, and visual confirmation. A server publication proves availability, not successful installation on every device. A heartbeat proves that the device is responding, not that its update task is enabled.
The printed notice can be removed only after a person verifies the relevant visitor display. The records provide that verification for both affected screens, but at different times. Do not give both screens the same repair time merely because they showed the same old package initially.
Follow-up work may include monitoring activation failures, auditing configuration changes, and checking whether a failed update produces an alert. Propose checks that distinguish the possible causes.

Task
List six key events in chronological order with dates, times, and record IDs. Explain the supported cause for each affected screen and identify remaining uncertainties. State when each screen was confirmed correct and which actions were temporary mitigation. Finish with two targeted follow-up checks, including the evidence each would collect.

category: 长上下文·英文规则判断
prompt:
Apply the rules of this fictional community room program and answer in English. Do not introduce outside regulations, assumed exceptions, or extra staff.

Facilities and calendar
The center has a small room and a large room. The small room holds at most twelve participants; the large room holds at most twenty-four. An adult supervisor counts as a participant for capacity. Staff who only unlock the building and leave do not count.
All requested dates are weekdays in May, and the rooms may be occupied from 09:00 through 18:00. There is no need to look up real dates or holidays. Times describe local clock time, and an interval ending at 15:00 does not overlap one starting at 15:00.

Rules
R1: A registered resident aged eighteen or older must submit each application and remain responsible for the group. A different adult may supervise on the day only if the application names that person and the center approves the substitution before the event.

R2: The declared participant count must fit the selected room. Furniture changes do not increase capacity. Children count individually, including children sharing a seat with a parent. No waiting group may occupy the corridor.

R3: Every reservation includes fifteen minutes of setup before the stated activity start and thirty minutes of cleanup after its stated finish. These intervals occupy the same room and must fit opening hours. Consecutive bookings are permitted only if their complete occupancy intervals do not overlap.

R4: Any activity with participants younger than sixteen requires an approved adult supervisor present throughout. That supervisor must be included in the count. A sixteen- or seventeen-year-old may participate without this special supervisor, but cannot be the responsible applicant under R1.

R5: Ordinary reading, discussion, and board-game activities require no deposit. An activity using paint, glue, or wet craft materials requires a 100-credit refundable deposit. The deposit is based on materials, not the group's size or whether the event is free.

R6: Amplified sound is forbidden in both rooms. Acoustic music is permitted only in the large room. The term acoustic means no powered speaker, microphone, or electronic amplification. A promise to keep a powered speaker quiet does not satisfy this rule.

R7: An application is not approved merely because a payment arrived or the room appears empty. Approval requires a complete responsible-person record, a feasible occupancy interval, capacity compliance, and compliance with the activity rules.

R8: Staff cannot waive these conditions verbally. A proposed change is not an accepted change until the applicant confirms it. When a request fails, identify the smallest necessary adjustment or missing evidence; do not report that adjustment as already completed.

Existing reservations
On May 12 the small room is occupied from 13:15 to 15:00, including setup and cleanup. The large room is occupied from 10:45 to 12:30, also including both buffers. Both rooms are otherwise free that day.
On May 14 the large room is occupied from 15:00 to 17:00, with buffers already included. The small room is free all day. Do not add a second pair of buffers to these existing occupancy intervals.

Applications
Case A: Mira, a registered adult resident, requests the small room on May 12 for a board-game activity from 12:00 to 13:00. Eleven adults will attend, including Mira. No craft materials or amplified sound will be used. The application is otherwise complete.

Case B: Jules, a registered adult resident, requests the large room on May 12 for painting from 13:00 to 15:00. Twenty-two children aged ten to twelve and two approved adult supervisors will attend. Jules is one supervisor and remains responsible. The 100-credit deposit has arrived. No audio equipment will be used.

Case C: Robin, a registered adult resident, requests the large room on May 14 for acoustic music from 13:30 to 14:45. Sixteen participants will attend, including Robin; the youngest is seventeen. The equipment list contains only unamplified instruments. The application is otherwise complete. Robin has suggested ending at 14:30 if necessary but has not confirmed a revision.

Task
For each case, state whether the submitted application can be approved, calculate its full occupancy interval, identify the applicable deposit, and cite the decisive rule numbers. Explain any overlap explicitly. For a case requiring a change, keep the requested activity start fixed and give the latest feasible earlier finish time under the existing bookings and distinguish that possible revision from the current request. Do not move another group's reservation or assume an unrequested room switch.

category: 长上下文·英文约束创作
prompt:
Write a complete short story in English using the fictional setting below. Aim for roughly 350 words of story. Read all the material before writing, preserve the established facts, and reveal the solution through actions and evidence rather than an explanatory lecture.

Place and time
An old riverside post office is being converted into a small community archive. It has been closed for twelve years. The sorting counter, pigeonholes, a mechanical wall clock, and a bicycle with a broken chain remain inside. It rains throughout this afternoon. Flooded roads prevent anyone from leaving the neighborhood before evening.
All discoveries must occur inside the post office, in the adjoining umbrella repair shop, or in the short covered passage between them. Do not introduce an online database, a distant expert arriving unexpectedly, a hidden tunnel to another town, or a journey that the flood would make impossible.

The protagonist
Nora is cataloguing objects for the archive. She records damage, ownership claims, and unanswered questions on separate cards. She is patient with uncertain evidence but impatient with a local rumor that her late father abandoned an important parcel on his final delivery round.
Her father was a postal carrier and died several years ago. He cannot return alive, call her on the telephone, or leave a newly written note. Nora has one genuine notebook of his, donated to the archive before today's work. Its dates and handwriting have already been checked. It contains routine delivery information, not a complete explanation of the mystery.

Other characters
Eli runs the umbrella repair shop. He was a teenager when the post office closed. He remembers watching the carriers but freely admits that his memory is incomplete. He owns the shop tools, not the objects inside the post office.
You may include one archive colleague as a third speaking character. That colleague can help inspect or record an object but has no secret knowledge of the parcel. Use no more than three speaking characters. Background residents may appear without dialogue, but no new relative or eyewitness may solve the mystery for Nora.

Objects and established observations
Inside a damaged envelope, Nora finds a small unsigned map. It marks the post office, the repair shop, and five dots along the covered passage. The paper is ordinary wrapping paper. One corner is torn, and a blue stamp partly crosses the tear.
A loose drawer contains five numbered brass tags. They are location labels, not money, jewelry, or keys. Their stamped numbers follow the same order as the dots on the map.
The notebook lists five parcels moved out of a leaking storeroom on the same afternoon, twelve years earlier. Beside the entry is the phrase "dry side, labels retained." The entry does not say that the parcels were delivered.
A wall cabinet in the repair shop has five numbered shelves. Eli recalls his mother temporarily storing objects for neighbors, but he cannot say which parcels occupied the cabinet that day. The cabinet may be examined with his permission; Nora must not break into it or claim it belongs to the archive.

The actual resolution
The map records emergency storage locations used during a leak. It is not a treasure map or a route for smuggling. The brass tags link the dots to temporary shelf locations. At least one surviving receipt or label in the cabinet must connect a parcel from the notebook to its later collection.
The evidence may clear the claim that Nora's father simply abandoned that particular parcel. It does not prove that every delivery in his career was perfect, nor does it establish the fate of all five parcels. Leave one small, specific uncertainty open. Do not invent a valuable inheritance as a reward.
The unsigned map can remain unsigned. If Nora guesses who drew it, present that as a possibility unless the story supplies actual supporting evidence. A familiar habit or an emotional impression alone is not proof of authorship.

Handling the evidence
A wet label has stuck to the cabinet's wooden back. Nora must ask permission before moving anything, photograph the label in place, and allow it to dry before reading the fragile edge. Its parcel number is legible without chemical treatment. Eli may lend a clean tray, but cannot supply a missing notebook page or identify the sender from memory. Preserve the distinction between an observed number and a guessed explanation.

Narrative requirements
Give the story a clear opening, a turning point caused by examining evidence, and an ending that changes Nora's understanding. Connect at least two of the clues in visible action. The rain may create pressure to protect documents, but it must not magically reveal invisible writing or wash away the only evidence.
End with Nora revising an archive label so it accurately separates what is now known from what remains uncertain. Keep the ending restrained rather than declaring that every family question has been answered. Write the story itself, without an outline, a list of clues, or a separate moral afterward.
